questions.question:
Identify the sentence with correct inversion after a negative adverbial phrase.

A) Never have I seen such a beautiful sunset.
B) Rarely I have seen such a beautiful sunset.
C) Scarcely had I seen such a beautiful sunset.
D) Lately I have seen such a beautiful sunset.
options: Never have I seen such a beautiful sunset.
Rarely I have seen such a beautiful sunset.
Scarcely had I seen such a beautiful sunset.
Lately I have seen such a beautiful sunset.
questions.answer: Scarcely had I seen such a beautiful sunset.

questions.question:
Which sentence correctly uses a cleft sentence to emphasize the location?

A) It was in the garden that they first met.
B) It was the garden where they first met.
C) They first met in the garden, that is certain.
D) The garden was where they first met.
options: It was in the garden that they first met.
It was the garden where they first met.
They first met in the garden, that is certain.
The garden was where they first met.
questions.answer: It was in the garden that they first met.

questions.question:
Select the correct form of the conditional sentence expressing an unreal present situation.

A) If I were you, I would have taken that job.
B) If I was you, I would have taken that job.
C) If I had been you, I would have taken that job.
D) If I had been, I would have taken that job.
options: If I were you, I would have taken that job.
If I was you, I would have taken that job.
If I had been you, I would have taken that job.
If I had been, I would have taken that job.
questions.answer: If I were you, I would have taken that job.

questions.question:
Which sentence correctly uses the subjunctive mood to express a hypothetical wish?

A) I suggest that she goes to the doctor.
B) I insist that he be present at the meeting.
C) It is essential that we are prepared.
D) We demand that they should arrive on time.
options: I suggest that she goes to the doctor.
I insist that he be present at the meeting.
It is essential that we are prepared.
We demand that they should arrive on time.
questions.answer: I insist that he be present at the meeting.

questions.question:
Identify the sentence with correct ellipsis, maintaining grammatical agreement.

A) She likes dancing, but he doesn’t.
B) She likes dancing, and he doesn’t.
C) She likes dancing, but he do not.
D) She likes dancing, but he doesn’t too.
options: She likes dancing, but he doesn’t.
She likes dancing, and he doesn’t.
She likes dancing, but he do not.
She likes dancing, but he doesn’t too.
questions.answer: She likes dancing, but he doesn’t.
